faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulhakim?
faq.a: Abdulhakim is associated with Arabic. Abdulhakim is Arabic عَبْدُ الْحَكِيم (ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm), meaning 'servant of the Wise'.
Yes — the underlying form عَبْدُ الْحَكِيم is Arabic.
Abdulhakim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Abdulhakim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm is a compound of two Quranic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.
